html:
The Romanian Revolution was a revolt in December 1989 that began in Timișoara and overthrew Nicolae Ceaușescu, the only one of the revolutions of 1989 that ended in bloodshed and the execution of a leader.

On 16 December people in Timișoara gathered to protect the Hungarian pastor László Tőkés from eviction, and the protest grew. Troops fired on the crowds. On 21 December Ceaușescu's speech to a rally in Bucharest turned into protest, broadcast live. The next day the army changed sides and he fled by helicopter. About 1,100 people died, many after his fall in shooting whose origin is still unclear. A National Salvation Front of former communists led by Ion Iliescu took power. Romania later joined NATO and, in 2007, the European Union.
sum: The Romanian Revolution was a revolt in December 1989 that began in Timișoara and overthrew Nicolae Ceaușescu, the only one of the revolutions of 1989 that ended in bloodshed and the execution of a leader.
